messages:
maria: Quick question — trying to make a reproducible CI flow for rw CLI auth. Want ephemeral tokens stored in a file mounted in the job, but also sometimes we fall back to profiles in ~/.redwood/config. What's the recommended precedence and any gotchas with streaming + retries in scripts?

alex: short answer: env vars win over config files. If you set RW_CLI_TOKEN (or RW_PROFILE to point at a profile) the CLI will prefer that. For CI I usually inject a token into RW_CLI_TOKEN in the job and avoid writing to home.

sam: important gotcha: streaming endpoints + client retries can cause duplicate output if the client-side retry replays a streaming request. For non-idempotent streams either disable automatic retries in the client or add an idempotency key header when supported.

maria: thanks — how do people disable retries in the CLI? and is there a way to safely script a refresh so the token file rotates without race conditions?

alex: for the CLI you can set RW_CLI_RETRIES=0 to disable client retries, or pass `--no-retry` where available in our wrapper scripts. e.g. `export RW_CLI_RETRIES=0 && rw chat stream --model gptx ...`

jin: for token rotation pattern we do this in our CI: write new token to a path mounted as a secret, then `mv` into place with atomic rename so readers either see old or new token. example: 
```sh
# assume /secrets/new_token mounted by vault
cat /secrets/new_token > /tmp/token.tmp
chmod 600 /tmp/token.tmp
mv /tmp/token.tmp /workspace/.rw_token
# export to process that needs it
export RW_CLI_TOKEN=$(cat /workspace/.rw_token)
rw api call ...
```
Atomic mv avoids partial reads.

sam: also if multiple processes might read concurrently, prefer a small wrapper that reads the token into env and execs the real command to avoid long-lived file reads: `RW_CLI_TOKEN=$(cat /workspace/.rw_token) rw ...`

maria: nice. And for fallbacks to profiles: if RW_PROFILE is set it will load that profile from `~/.redwood/config`, right? Any interaction with RW_CLI_TOKEN?

alex: precedence: explicit env token (RW_CLI_TOKEN) > RW_PROFILE pointing to a profile > default profile in config. If both RW_CLI_TOKEN and RW_PROFILE are present, the env token takes priority. So for CI set RW_CLI_TOKEN to be explicit and you won't accidentally use a dev profile.

maria: good to know. One more — streaming healthcheck: I sometimes see partial output then a retry which restarts the stream. Any server-side headers we can use to detect a resumed stream vs new one?

sam: server sends `x-rw-session-id` on streaming connections — you can log that on the client. If a retry creates a new session id it's a fresh stream. For resumable streams we'd need explicit cursor support which the server doesn't provide today. So disabling retries for streaming is the right pattern.

maria: thanks! i'll implement RW_CLI_RETRIES=0 for streaming steps and use atomic mv token rotation for other jobs.

deploy-bot: scheduled job `weekly-canary` started (job id: 6721) :rocket:

jin: FYI if you need to exchange a service account for short-lived tokens in CI we have an internal endpoint `rw auth:exchange` — will share snippet if you want it to plug into the mv pattern.

maria: please share, that would be perfect. thanks all :thank_you:
